plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 5-date timeline completes: 1738 (French Academy cannon-flash experiments clock sound at 331 m/s at 0 °C) · 25 May 1842 (Christian Doppler presents his wave-shift equation in Prague) · 3–5 Jun 1845 (Buys Ballot's Utrecht steam-train horn experiment) · 1868 (William Huggins measures the first stellar Doppler shift in Sirius) · 1887 (Ernst Mach & Peter Salcher photograph the supersonic bullet shockwave cone), alongside an inked diagram of a supersonic aircraft dragging a continuous Mach shockwave wake across the ground and 1957 Doppler medical ultrasound.

teach_overlay.scale: a supersonic jet at Mach 2 drags a continuous cone of compressed air across the ground at nearly seven hundred metres per second — twice as fast as a rifle shot
teach_overlay.fact_card: Sonic booms never stop in flight
